onboarding.title: What are you managing?
onboarding.lede: This helps us show you the right reminders and information. You can change this later.
onboarding.prescription_lede: How many days does your current prescription cover?
onboarding.footer_note: Everything you enter stays on your phone unless you choose to share it later.

home.checkin_question: Did you take your medication today?
home.checkin_completed_body: Thank you for updating your routine!

readings.lede_bp: Enter the numbers from your monitor.
readings.lede_glucose: Enter your blood sugar value from your glucometer.

emergency.body_bp: This is high or low enough that it needs medical attention right away. Please contact a health worker or go to a facility now.
emergency.body_low_glucose: This is dangerously low. If you have fast-acting sugar (juice, glucose tablets, regular soda), take it now and recheck in 15 minutes. If you feel confused or cannot treat yourself, get help immediately.
emergency.body_high_glucose: This is dangerously high — please contact a health worker or go to a facility now, especially if you feel unwell, confused, or notice fruity-smelling breath.
emergency.footer_note: This message cannot be dismissed without confirming you have seen it.

escalation.title: Check-in support
escalation.lede: If you'd like, a trusted person can be gently notified if we don't hear from you for a while. This is completely optional and off by default.
escalation.toggle_status_off: Currently off. Turning this on will ask you to choose a contact below.
escalation.toggle_status_on: Currently enabled. Your trusted contact will only receive a check-in alert if you miss 7 consecutive days.
escalation.what_they_see_lede: Only this message — never your readings, adherence, or medication details:
escalation.sample_preview: "Hi, this is a check-in reminder from {name}'s health app. They haven't logged an update in a week — it might be worth checking in with them."

education.card1_title: Why keep tracking, even on good days?
education.card1_body: Blood pressure and blood sugar can rise quietly without any symptoms. Regular readings catch changes early — not how you feel day to day.
education.card2_title: Feeling healthy means treatment is working
education.card2_body: When you feel energetic and strong, that is evidence your medication is doing its protective job. Keep the momentum going!
education.card3_body: Refilling a few days before your last tablet ensures you never have a gap day. Your local dispensary or chemist can assist you.
education.card4_body: Managing chronic health is a long journey. Every single day of taking care of yourself protects your heart, brain, kidneys, and eyes.
